newsitem.title: JORDAN: Netanyahu is no joke for Jordan's comedians.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu is no joke for Jordan's comedians.

text.p: Jordan's most famous comedy double-act has cancelled a performance in Israel, saying on Wednesday that Arabs and Israelis had nothing to laugh about while violence escalated in the West Bank.

Political satirists "Nabil and Hisham", who broke an Arab taboo on cultural ties with Israel when they took their show to the Jewish state two years ago, said they pulled out to protest the policies of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"We feel Netanyahu just doesn't want peace, so we don't want normal ties with Israel any more," said Nabil Sawalha, who makes up the comedy duo with Hisham Yannis.
They cancelled a planned show in Tel Aviv next month after Netanyahu started building Jewish settlements in Arab East Jerusalem, sparking Palestinian anger and international condemnation.
"These people live in cuckoo-land, they are horrifying," Sawalha said of Netanyahu's right-wing government.
He said a breakdown of Israeli-Palestinian talks and rising violence in the West Bank left little room for humour.
"Netanyahu is no longer funny to me," he told Reuters. "We like to laugh at everyone, but the mood just isn't right".

Jokes about Netanyahu's 'peace' strategy ("Palestinians are like photographs -- shoot them first and see what develops") fell a bit flat while Palestinians were being shot dead by Israeli soldiers in the West Bank, he said.
"We were one of the first (Arab) acts to perform in Israel... I risked a lot to move this peace process and the return was entirely negative," he said.

The comedians' boycott reflects a groundswell of anti-Israeli feeling in Jordan, which had gone much further than other Arab states towards normalising relations with Israel since it signed a 1994 peace treaty with its former foe.

Jordanian lawyers have rushed to defend a Jordanian soldier who shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls last month after King Hussein warned Netanyahu he was pushing the Middle East towards an "abyss of violence".
An Israeli diplomat's car was vandalised in Amman in March and last week police arrested at least 10 teenage students who said they had demonstrated against the Israeli embassy.
"The feelings against us would be very strong if we went to Israel," Sawalha said. "Even the ordinary man does not believe in peace with Israel now".
